stories.headline: Fireworks AI Raises $1.5 Billion Series D at a $17.5 Billion Valuation as Enterprises Flee Frontier API Pricing
stories.key_takeaway: Fireworks' $1.505B Series D at a $17.5B valuation — a 4x markup in nine months on $1B ARR and 40 trillion daily tokens — marks investors betting that the inference and fine-tuning layer, not the model layer, is where enterprise AI lock-in forms.

pull_quote.text: There are two paths forward for AI. In one, intelligence belongs to a few big labs, and everyone else rents it. In the other, every company in the world builds specialized intelligence of its own, shaped by the domain only it understands. We are building towards the second.

stories.article_excerpt: Fireworks, the San Mateo inference platform founded by the engineers who built PyTorch, has raised a $1.505 billion Series D at a $17.5 billion valuation.

stories.headline: HappyRobot Raises $150 Million and Crosses Into Unicorn Territory on Logistics AI Agents
stories.key_takeaway: HappyRobot hit a $1.2B valuation just 20 months after its first institutional round by automating the calls, emails and handoffs that freight brokers run on — evidence that vertical AI agents in multi-step operational workflows, not horizontal chat assistants, are where enterprise capital is now flowing.

pull_quote.text: Many industries have a surprising share of their costs locked up in coordination, the calls, emails, and handoffs that keep work flowing. While getting an agent to complete a discrete task is increasingly simple, deploying them across multi-step enterprise workflows has proven far more difficult.

stories.headline: IQVIA's Agentic AI Platform Scales to 294 Deployed Agents, Nearly Doubling Since Its March Launch
stories.key_takeaway: IQVIA launched IQVIA.ai in March with 150+ agents deployed; by its July 28 earnings call the count had reached 294 agents across 90 use cases, with 19 of the top 20 pharma companies using them — making clinical development one of the first heavily regulated domains where agentic AI runs at production scale.

pull_quote.text: By bringing together our data, expertise and Healthcare-grade AI within a unified, agentic platform, IQVIA.ai enables organizations to move faster and smarter while meeting the rigorous standards of trust and reliability that are required in the industry.
pull_quote.role: Senior Vice President, AI and Technology Solutions, IQVIA

stories.headline: Samsung's HBM4 Yields Reportedly Reach 80%, but the Number Is Single-Sourced
stories.key_takeaway: Samsung's reported 80% HBM4 yield traces to a single unnamed source in Seoul Economic Daily and is unconfirmed by the company, but corroborating disclosures support the direction. A credible Samsung second source will not lower HBM prices through 2027 — it buys buyers negotiating position in a market where memory, not logic, gates accelerator supply.

pull_quote.text: Agentic AI is a new kind of workload. One prompt can launch a thousand-step journey of reasoning, retrieval, tool use and response generation. Vera Rubin was built for this moment — an AI factory engine that delivers intelligence at scale.

stories.headline: Google's Gemini 3.7 Flash Targets Coding and Agents With a 50% Introductory Price Cut
stories.key_takeaway: Google shipped Gemini 3.7 Flash just three weeks after 3.6 Flash, leading FrontierCode and AutomationBench while undercutting rivals — but the 50% cut is a promotion against unchanged list pricing that expires December 31, 2026, and independent testing puts the real cost-per-task improvement at 30%.

pull_quote.text: The more important development is the continued compression of the price of useful machine intelligence. Capability, latency and cost are becoming inseparable buying criteria.

stories.article_excerpt: Three weeks is not a product cycle. It is barely a sprint. But three weeks is exactly how long Gemini 3.6 Flash held the top of Google's workhorse lineup.

stories.headline: ByteDance's Cheapest Frontier Model Slips Into Western APIs at $0.50 per Million Tokens
stories.key_takeaway: Seed 2.1 Turbo did not launch in August — it debuted in China on June 23 at Volcano Engine FORCE and only reached Western aggregators around August 10-12 at $0.50/$2.50 per million tokens with a 262K context. ByteDance has published no Turbo-specific benchmarks and no parameter count: a frontier-class price with unverified frontier-class capability.

pull_quote.text: The reason we cut prices in 2024 was because all models could only do Chatbot — the models were only worth that price.

stories.headline: DARPA and the Air Force Fly a Frontline F-16 Under AI Control at Eglin
stories.key_takeaway: A standard fleet F-16 flew portions of test sorties under AI control at Eglin AFB in July 2026 — the point is not that software flew a fighter, which happened on the one-off X-62A VISTA in 2022, but that it flew an ordinary operational jet via a bolt-on kit, creating a repeatable pipeline into the Air Force's Collaborative Combat Aircraft programs.

pull_quote.text: Many hard questions remain concerning the performance and trustworthiness of combat AI in the extreme fog and friction of modern warfare.

stories.headline: Epistemic Context Learning Teaches AI Agents Which of Their Peers to Trust
stories.key_takeaway: ECL makes an agent build a natural-language reliability profile of its peers from five rounds of interaction history before seeing the current question — letting Qwen 3-4B beat a history-agnostic aggregator eight times its size. The gains are large against deceptive peers and near-zero against cooperative ones, and the paper's own Flip test shows agents collapse when a trusted peer turns unreliable.

pull_quote.text: When correctness cannot be established from the current interaction alone, the problem naturally shifts from evaluating what is said to evaluating who is speaking.
pull_quote.attribution: Ruiwen Zhou, Maojia Song and co-authors
pull_quote.role: Authors of Epistemic Context Learning, arXiv:2601.21742

data_points.label: Qwen 3-4B with ECL vs Qwen 3-30B without

stories.headline: 'Agentic AI Scientists Are Not Built for Autonomous Scientific Discovery,' a New Paper Argues
stories.key_takeaway: A May 2026 position paper from IIT Delhi and Friedrich Schiller University Jena argues agentic AI scientists fail at autonomous discovery for reasons inherent to how they are trained — biased problem selection, missing tacit knowledge, preference optimisation that compresses hypothesis diversity — not for lack of scale, and backs the diversity claim with a six-model experiment showing frontier models from rival labs converge semantically.

pull_quote.text: A research community that queries multiple AI systems for novel hypotheses is, from an epistemic standpoint, effectively sampling from a single model.
pull_quote.attribution: Bisht, Kumar, Jablonka, Mausam and Krishnan

data_points.label: Scale of the hypothesis hivemind experiment
Evidence ignored vs belief revised, 25,000+ runs
GNoME crystal structures experimentally realized
Narrowing of scientific topic volume under AI adoption

stories.article_excerpt: Most critiques of AI scientists argue the systems are not good enough yet. A position paper posted to arXiv on May 9 makes a harder claim: that they are built wrong.

stories.headline: LLMs Can Reason Deep. A New Benchmark Asks Whether They Can Reason Wide.
stories.key_takeaway: MPAR-Bench, a 1,000-item English-Chinese benchmark built on the party game Just One, tests whether models can converge several unrelated clues onto one hidden word. Gemini-3.1pro leads at 86.8% English / 72.2% Chinese, but simple perturbations cost every model 9-18 points in English, and reasoning traces contain logical errors 20-44% of the time even when the answer is right.

pull_quote.text: Improving breadth appears challenging: scaling model size, adding reasoning strategies, and iterative feedback each bring only partial gains, suggesting that reasoning breadth may be a capability that current training paradigms do not naturally optimize for.
pull_quote.attribution: Si'an Xie, Jiaxun Liu and co-authors
pull_quote.role: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Peking University and Kuaishou, arXiv:2608.10444

data_points.label: Best accuracy (Gemini-3.1pro) on English / Chinese

stories.article_excerpt: The last two years of language-model progress have been a story about going deeper. But there is a second kind of reasoning almost nobody scores.

stories.headline: Judge Grants Final Approval to Anthropic's $1.5 Billion Copyright Settlement, the Largest in U.S. Copyright History
stories.key_takeaway: The court approved a record $1.5B payout at roughly $3,000 per work with a deliberately narrow release covering only past acquisition and copying through August 25, 2025 — leaving output claims, future conduct, and the industry-wide fair-use question entirely unresolved.

pull_quote.text: A lot of travel, a lot of discussion about what to do and how to proceed and a lot of jobs passed up. I'm much poorer for this settlement, ironically.

stories.headline: No, the FDA Didn't Create an 'Autonomous Diagnostic AI' Class — But the Line Moved Anyway in 2026
stories.key_takeaway: The FDA did not create an 'Autonomous Diagnostic AI' class — no such classification exists, and autonomous diagnostics have been authorized since IDx-DR in 2018. What actually changed in 2026 is the FDA's January deregulation of clinical decision support software, the first FDA-cleared patient-facing clinical LLM, and Utah's state-level prescription-renewal sandbox now under attack from the state medical board and the AMA.

pull_quote.text: The story is not that FDA cleared an autonomous LLM physician (it did not).

stories.headline: UK Confirms Mandatory AI Chatbot Breaks for Under-18s and Default Midnight Curfews for Older Teens
stories.key_takeaway: The UK's 15 July 2026 DSIT package is not new primary legislation but a consultation response to be delivered via regulations under the Online Safety Act: mandatory breaks for under-18s using AI chatbots, default midnight-to-6am curfews and autoplay restrictions for 16- and 17-year-olds that teens can switch off, and explicitly no VPN ban.

pull_quote.text: We will therefore require mandatory breaks for under-18s using chatbots and will work with experts on how frequently, and for how long, these should happen.
pull_quote.role: Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology

stories.article_excerpt: Britain will require AI chatbot providers to force periodic breaks on users under 18, and will oblige social media services to switch on overnight curfews by default.

stories.headline: State Department Puts $50 Million Behind a Digital Passport for AI Chips — Starting in Panama
stories.key_takeaway: On August 12, 2026 the State Department opened a competitive funding solicitation for the Pax Silica AI Assistance Project, seeking up to $50 million to build an AI supply-chain credentialing and provenance platform with Panama's ports and customs authorities — an attempt to give export controls working plumbing at a chokepoint carrying roughly 3% of global maritime trade.

pull_quote.text: If the 20th century was built on oil and steel, the 21st century is built on computing and the minerals that power it.
pull_quote.role: U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs
